chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Playing for the Charioteers and at the Famous Door
summary: Wilson accompanied the Charioteers on network radio and played intermission piano at the Famous Door on 52nd Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And out of that, I began to play for an excellent group from Cincinnati that had come to New York called the Charioteers, a singing group.
Oh yeah! Specs Odum was the piano player for them.
No, I was the piano player for them.
You were? I'm thinking of another group, then.

Sure. Billie Williams. And these fellows had quite a variety of vocal arrangements, and were very busy with radio. We were on the radio five times a week; they had three days a week for commercial, for a vapor rub product,

cold remedies and things like that -- we were on NBC three days a week and two days a week on WOR, the mutual network, and I was playing for those guys, and also I was the intermission piano player at the Famous Door on 52nd Street -- the first of the jazz clubs, and it had gotten opened by a bunch of musicians; I think Lennie Hayton was one of them; a lot of musicians went together and bought this little place.
What was the name of it?
Oh yeah. Ralph Watkins. Was he....?

No, that was before Ralph. I'm going back to about 1934-35 now, and I was the house piano player there; I used to play solo there at intermissions, and Louie Prima was there for awhile and Bunny Berigan had a small group there with Joe Bushkin on piano, and Wingy Manone's little band was in there while the period I played with them -- I played intermissions, rather.
